import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Domains keep their data apart. Brightwater's `rentals` domain shows a booking
with the client's name on it, but the client lives in the `clients` domain.
Two tools open a controlled door between domains. A **domain grant** is a
consent contract: the producing domain names a consumer and the resources it
may read. A **replicated field** copies one value from a source document into
the consumer's document, so the consumer shows it without a lookup.

## When to use this

- A doctype references documents in another domain and its scripts must read
  them.
- A list in the `rentals` domain should show a value that lives in
  `clients`, such as the client's name.
- You want the copy to follow the source automatically.

## Before you start

- **Two sides.** Decide which side holds the contract: the **producer** gives
  data, the **consumer** receives it.
- **Tags.** [Tag](/admin/people/hidden-fields/) the producer fields you share. A field without tags carries
  the implicit tag `default`.
- **Read only.** Grants give read access only. No grant ever allows a write.
- **Same domain needs none.** Two doctypes inside one domain read each other
  without a grant. The grant is the contract between domains.

## Steps

A grant is a document, not a definition, so domain files carry none — the
steps below are the same work in the app and through the API.

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the producer domain's document page — the grant lives there, as a
   child of the domain.
2. Create one grant per consumer domain. Name the consumer, and add one
   resource entry per doctype with the tags the consumer may read.
3. Have a holder of the producer's **Activate** right turn the grant on.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="API">

The grant is a document under the producer domain. Brightwater files one so
`rentals` may read `clients`:

```sh
curl -k -X POST "https://facet.localhost:3443/Api/core/Domain/clients/grants" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FACET_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "consumer_domain": "core.Domain.rentals",
    "resources": [
      { "doctype": "Company", "tags": ["default"] }
    ]
  }'

curl -k -X POST "https://facet.localhost:3443/Api/core/DomainGrant/<grant-id>/activate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FACET_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

`-k` skips the certificate check of the local development address. A new
grant starts inactive; an inactive grant admits nothing. Facet refuses a
self-grant: a domain needs no contract to read itself.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Declare the replicated field on the consumer

On the consumer doctype, add two fields: a reference to the source doctype,
and a field that holds the copy. This is the real Brightwater booking:

```yaml
# rentals/doctypes/rentals.Booking.yml (extract)
fields:
  client:
    type: reference
    title: Client
    doctype: clients.Company
    required: true
    filters: [equality]
  client_name:
    type: string
    title: Client name
    replicate:
      via: client
      field: name
    filters: [text_search]
```

Rules for the pair:

- `via` names the reference field on the same doctype.
- The source field must not be a secret, and a copy cannot feed another copy.
- The copy must carry every tag its source carries.
- `on_source_delete` is `keep` (the default) or `unset`. `keep` leaves the
  copied value; `unset` clears it when the source is deleted.
- Users cannot write a copied field. It cannot be required or unique.

### Watch the copies behave

Facet pulls the initial value when a consumer document is created or its
reference changes. Later changes on the source push to every consumer that
references it. Each push is a real, audited update on the consumer document.

:::caution
A cross-domain edge without an active grant stays inert. The check reports
the missing grant, and the copy stays empty until the producer activates the
contract.
:::

## Example

The example instance carries the working pair. A booking references
`clients.Company.06H1FM1B3MXBPS0JYVM3BDD154`, whose name is `Maison
Lumière`. The booking shows the copy:

```json
{
  "client": "clients.Company.06H1FM1B3MXBPS0JYVM3BDD154",
  "client_name": "Maison Lumière",
  "status": "confirmed"
}
```

The client later renames. The copy on the booking updates without anyone
touching the booking, and the history shows the update as an automated
change on the booking.

## Troubleshooting

**The copy stays empty.**

Walk the chain: the grant must be active, it must name the source doctype,
and its tags must cover the source field. The doctype check names the
missing piece.

**The copy did not follow a source change.**

The reference must point at the source document. An empty or dangling
reference has no source to pull from.

**The grant disappeared from the consumer's view.**

A widened grant returns to inactive until the producer accepts it again. The
publish dialog reports this when it happens.
